Use case: illustration-story. Create FRAME 1 OF 4 of a seamless four-frame horror-game death-screen animation, a single standalone 16:9 landscape illustration, not a grid or contact sheet. Visual style: handmade wax-crayon drawing on worn tan corrugated cardboard, rough childlike crosshatched strokes, ochre bare-paper negative space, torn scuffed cardboard edges, flat paper-theatre cutout silhouettes, muted red yellow blue green crayons. Reference appearance described: a red striped circus tent, colorful triangular bunting and crudely drawn amusement park rides on rough brown cardboard. Apply that same visual language to this entirely new scene.
Scene: an abandoned amusement-park carousel at night, viewed from a locked front-facing wide camera. The carousel fills the central 70% of the frame; broad red-and-ochre scalloped canopy, central striped mast, oval wooden platform, four poles with toy horses; a small crayon ferris wheel and dark pine trees in the distant background. Distressed dark blue crayon sky on cardboard, sparse crooked yellow fairy lights. Keep the cardboard grain strong, shadows as charcoal crayon hatching. No photorealism, no 3D render.
Subject: a clearly ADULT male paranormal-investigator blogger, short dark hair, torn dark teal jacket, ochre T-shirt, charcoal trousers, brown shoes, a little camera dangling on his chest. His lifeless body is slumped unnaturally over a blue wooden carousel horse: head hanging down, back folded across the saddle, arms dangling, limp attached legs. Clothing ragged and silhouette contorted to suggest a terrible fate, but NO graphic injuries, NO exposed flesh wounds, NO gore, NO dismemberment, NO exposed bone or organs. All limbs remain attached. Not a child. The horse and body must be fully visible in a medium-wide scene, not a close-up. The death is conveyed through stillness, posture and empty atmosphere.
Animation plan: fixed identical background, canopy and platform in every frame. Only carousel horses and the limp body change location and bob slightly. This FRAME 1 has the occupied blue horse on the FRONT-LEFT quarter of the oval, body at about 39% image width and 61% image height. The other horses: small red horse front-right, yellow rear-left, green rear-right. Keep a clear recognizable silhouette, crisp enough for a game background. Reserve upper 15% sky for possible later UI; do not add any text, letters, numbers, watermarks, UI or frame labels. One image only, landscape 16:9.
